policy_name: Building a Responsible Humanitarian Approach: The ICRC's Policy on Artificial Intelligence
issuing_authority: International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC)
regulatory_regime: Organisational AI policy of a humanitarian organisation (alongside the binding ICRC Rules on Personal Data Protection)
geo_constraints: All ICRC staff, activities, internal services, operational responses and partnerships worldwide

locale_context.region: Global (corporate) › International Committee of the Red Cross
locale_context.regulation: Internal policy · principles-based, aspirational organisational AI framework
locale_context.culture: Humanitarian-principles framing (humanity, impartiality, neutrality, independence, do no harm): AI use is weighed against risks to people affected by conflict and to the ICRC's perceived neutrality, with precaution and data protection foremost.

versions.title: Ref. 4837/002, November 2024
versions.summary: Only one version recorded for this policy.

covered_entities: AI providers (through procurement and ethical frameworks)
covered_systems: existing tools that add AI functionality
covered_activities: exploration, deployment, use and management of AI
procurement and choice of AI providers
use of external online AI services
exceptions: does not address the ICRC's position on the use of AI by parties to armed conflict under IHL
conditions: additional risk analysis for higher-risk solutions or those using personal, confidential or sensitive data
objective: Provide a value-based, principled framework for the ICRC's human-centred, responsible and ethical exploration and use of AI in humanitarian action, consistent with its mandate and Fundamental Principles.
principles: proportionality, precaution and do no harm

related_policies.policy: ICRC Rules on Personal Data Protection
Handbook on Data Protection in Humanitarian Action

conflict_rule: Complements, and is without prejudice to, the ICRC Rules on Personal Data Protection, which are binding on the organisation (s.3).

record_provenance.notes: Text taken from the copy in asago-ai/asago-policy-mapper (policy_examples/icrc.pdf). (asago-ai/asago-policy-mapper commit b8ac8876beec6593ef5685d7d7e64cc94f9cc55b.) Publication month only (November 2024); no exact day or version number beyond the print reference 4837/002 11.2024. The policy calls itself 'aspirational' and 'a living instrument that will be regularly updated', so status is recorded as voluntary although it is the ICRC's own internal policy; not verified whether a later update exists. The -layout extraction interleaves columns, so clauses were taken from a plain pdftotext re-extraction; footnote 1 (the source of the AI definition) is not legible in the text layer. The prohibited-practices list in s.5.1 closely mirrors EU AI Act Article 5, though the policy only cites the Act among its sources. Binding=false: not law; the policy is addressed to all ICRC staff.

clauses.section: 5.1 A humanitarian and principled approach – Humanity
clauses.original_text: In light of the above, the ICRC will refrain from using, deploying or providing AI systems that: deploy subliminal, manipulative, or deceptive techniques to distort behaviour and impair informed decision-making; exploit vulnerabilities related to age, disability, or socio-economic circumstances to distort behaviour; use biometric categorization systems that infer sensitive personal attributes, except for labelling or filtering lawfully acquired biometric datasets; rely on or infer social scoring, (i.e. evaluating or classifying individuals or groups based on social behaviour or personal traits); assess the risk of an individual committing a criminal offence based solely on profiling or personality traits, except when used to augment human assessments; compile facial recognition databases by untargeted scraping of facial images from the internet or CCTV footage; or infer emotions, except for medical or safety reasons.
clauses.action: refrain from using, deploying or providing
clauses.object: manipulative, exploitative, biometric-categorisation, social-scoring, predictive-policing, facial-scraping and emotion-recognition AI systems
clauses.requirement: do not use, deploy or provide listed prohibited categories of AI
clauses.exception: labelling/filtering lawfully acquired biometric datasets; risk assessment that augments human assessment; emotion inference for medical or safety reasons
clauses.purpose: protect dignity, agency and rights of affected people
clauses.affected_asset: affected people's autonomy, privacy and rights
clauses.applicable_systems: AI systems used, deployed or provided by the ICRC
clauses.interpretation_notes: Text from a plain pdftotext re-extraction of the asago PDF (two-column layout); line breaks and hyphenation joined, bullet markers dropped. List closely mirrors EU AI Act Art. 5 prohibitions, with similar carve-outs.

clauses.section: 5.1 A humanitarian and principled approach – Impartiality
clauses.original_text: The ICRC acknowledges the significant risks of AI systems that could generate false or inaccurate data and replicate or amplify systemic and societal discriminations, biases and stereotypes – in particular around gender and race. We make proactive and sustained efforts to understand, avoid and mitigate these risks through our choice and use of AI solutions, and by avoiding their use where these biases cannot be effectively avoided or mitigated.
clauses.action: understand, avoid and mitigate; avoid use
clauses.object: bias, discrimination and inaccuracy in AI systems
clauses.requirement: mitigate bias and inaccuracy; do not use AI where bias cannot be effectively mitigated
clauses.affected_asset: affected populations (especially regarding gender and race)
clauses.applicable_systems: AI solutions chosen and used by the ICRC
clauses.interpretation_notes: Text from a plain pdftotext re-extraction of the asago PDF (two-column layout); line breaks and hyphenation joined, bullet markers dropped. Framed as a commitment ('we make … efforts'); the refusal to use AI where bias cannot be mitigated is close to a MUST NOT.

clauses.original_text: At all times, the ICRC ensures that confidential or sensitive internal ICRC information or personal data are handled with the utmost care and are not used in or transferred to non-approved, external online AI systems, in line with the duty of discretion stated in the ICRC’s Code of Conduct.
clauses.object: confidential or sensitive internal information or personal data
clauses.requirement: no confidential/sensitive information or personal data in non-approved external online AI systems
clauses.affected_asset: confidential ICRC information; personal data of affected people
clauses.interpretation_notes: Text from a plain pdftotext re-extraction of the asago PDF (two-column layout); line breaks and hyphenation joined, bullet markers dropped. s.6.4 adds that staff must not input critical humanitarian, (strictly) confidential or IP-protected information into external or commercial online AI services.

clauses.original_text: Additional systematic data quality control and meaningful and effective human oversight mechanisms are put in place to control and review relevant training models, algorithmic systems, inputs and outputs throughout the lifecycle of AI solutions used to support operational activities and decision-making processes that have an impact and present a risk of harm for affected people and users.
clauses.action: put in place human oversight and data quality control
clauses.object: training models, algorithmic systems, inputs and outputs
clauses.requirement: meaningful human oversight and data quality control throughout the lifecycle of impactful AI
clauses.condition: where AI supports operational activities or decisions that have an impact and present a risk of harm
clauses.applicable_systems: AI supporting operational activities and decision-making with risk of harm
clauses.interpretation_notes: Text from a plain pdftotext re-extraction of the asago PDF (two-column layout); line breaks and hyphenation joined, bullet markers dropped. Descriptive present tense in an aspirational policy; read as SHOULD.

clauses.original_text: Relevant and intelligible information about the use of AI systems is systematically provided to affected people and users when these systems could have an impact on them or their rights, or when decisions with significant consequences for the organization are concerned.
clauses.requirement: inform affected people and users about AI use where it may affect them or their rights
clauses.condition: when systems could impact them or their rights, or for decisions with significant consequences for the organization
clauses.purpose: transparency and accountability to affected people
clauses.applicable_systems: AI systems that could impact affected people or their rights
clauses.interpretation_notes: Text from a plain pdftotext re-extraction of the asago PDF (two-column layout); line breaks and hyphenation joined, bullet markers dropped. The next bullet extends this to why, when and how AI is used and explanations of the input-output link.

clauses.original_text: All possible efforts are made to integrate and mitigate the environmental impact and carbon footprint of considered AI solutions through a life-cycle approach. This includes favouring solutions and tools that have a lighter footprint, in line with the ICRC’s Plan of Action under the Climate and Environment Charter for Humanitarian Organizations and the ICRC’s Framework for Sustainable Development.
clauses.action: mitigate environmental impact; favour lighter-footprint tools
clauses.requirement: life-cycle mitigation of AI environmental impact and carbon footprint
clauses.applicable_systems: AI solutions considered by the ICRC
clauses.interpretation_notes: Text from a plain pdftotext re-extraction of the asago PDF (two-column layout); line breaks and hyphenation joined, bullet markers dropped.
